story.head: Stay out of the box, Blue Jackets
paras: The Devils (15-8-0) lost 9-6 to St. Louis on Saturday, while the Blue Jackets have won two in a row. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Blue Jackets seventh (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Devils second (tenth).

The Blue Jackets have played better than their record (.429) says: their chances are worth about .499, and their finishing has held them back. So have the Devils (.652 on chances worth .730), where their goaltending has held them back.

The Blue Jackets do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest) and lean hard on their top players (4th lowest). They also get their defensemen shooting (3rd), so their defensemen shoot a lot, and the Devils’ not so much. Columbus has scored 2.48 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Devils draw more penalties than they take (2nd), rarely throw hits (2nd lowest) and keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest). New Jersey has scored 3.78 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. The Devils’ power play (5th) could do real damage against the Jackets’ penalty kill (24th).

Kent Johnson (9 G / 13 A / 22 P in 21 GP) leads the Blue Jackets in scoring, and Zach Werenski (5 G / 15 A / 20 P in 21 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Devils, Jack Hughes (10 G / 19 A / 29 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in five straight games against Columbus. Jesper Bratt (4 G / 18 A / 22 P in 23 GP) isn’t far behind.
Cam Talbot (7-4-0 / .905 SV% in 11 GS) is expected to start for Columbus, and Connor Hellebuyck (7-1-0 / .897 SV% in 9 GS) for New Jersey.
At home, Sheldon Keefe likes to send Meier, Hischier and Evangelista out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Knies, Bel Belluz and Johnson.
